steps: GET http://127.0.0.1:3002/landing and read Content-Security-Policy (dev variant).
title: Frontend content policy allows inline scripts in production
expected: Production CSP uses per-request nonces or hashes for scripts (no 'unsafe-inline'), restricts img-src to known hosts, and the framework banner is off.
actual: Production script-src is 'self' 'unsafe-inline' plus Google, Stripe and Sentry CDN; img-src allows any https: origin; X-Powered-By: Next.js is sent. (Dev adds 'unsafe-eval', which is expected.) The backend API, by contrast, has a deny-all CSP and HSTS in production. Confirmed in production on 2026-11-05: same script-src with 'unsafe-inline' (no 'unsafe-eval') and X-Powered-By: Next.js.
impact: An injected script (stored XSS in user content) would run; CSP provides little protection. ADR-004 lists CSP as an XSS mitigation.
fix: Generate a nonce in proxy.ts and pass it to Next.js (supported in Next 16 — read node_modules/next/dist/docs first), switch script-src to 'self' 'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'; list image hosts explicitly; set poweredByHeader: false. Roll out with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first.
